# goalify

> A Claude Code / Agent Skills skill that preps a big coding task while the current session still has
> the user's context. It turns the task into two artifacts: a **brief** — a self-contained
> implementation file the fresh session works from — and a **condition** — the `/goal` string derived
> from that brief's definition of done. It researches the task, locks the few real decisions (asking
> the user only the genuine forks, one interactive MCQ), and wires the finish line to commands the run
> can check, so the user can `/clear`, paste the condition into `/goal`, and have a fresh, full-context
> session prove every criterion before it stops. The brief is archived on success. MIT licensed.

goalify solves a specific, unresolved problem: carrying a plan across `/clear` into a fresh
implementation session (Claude Code issue #32916, "Best practice for plan-to-implementation context
handoff across /clear?", raised on Anthropic's tracker and closed as not planned, with no documented
best practice). It is a two-phase model: PREPARE (research, decide, author the file, in the current
session) then EXECUTE (the user pastes the derived condition into `/goal` in a fresh session). It
authors the handoff; it does not run the task itself. For immediate in-session execution, use autopilot/ultrawork/ralph.

The brief is hardened with the patterns most autonomous runs miss: a declarative spec,
machine-checkable success criteria wired to named commands, a separate-agent verification pass,
fan-out guardrails (parallel for independent discovery/verify; serialize builds/tests/same-file
writes), output-redirection, anti-placeholder and search-before-assuming rules, a resumable progress
checklist, and a low-freedom gated archive step that fires only on full success.

Since v2.0.0 goalify emits two artifacts, because `/goal` takes a **completion condition, not a file
path** (docs: "Run `/goal` followed by the condition you want satisfied"; binary: `No goal set. Usage:
/goal <condition>`; the evaluator has no tools and cannot read files). The brief is what the worker
implements; the derived, linted condition string is what the user pastes into `/goal`. Codex's `/goal`
also takes an inline objective rather than a path, so both forms are printed — but Codex wraps the
objective as untrusted data, so only the definition of done binds there, not the process directives.

## Docs

- [README](https://github.com/Aboudjem/goalify/blob/main/README.md): What goalify is, who it is for, how to install and use it.
- [SKILL.md](https://github.com/Aboudjem/goalify/blob/main/skills/goalify/SKILL.md): The skill definition — two-phase model, procedure, the brief template, the one-vs-several decision, the handoff format, and hard rules.
- [Quickstart](https://github.com/Aboudjem/goalify/blob/main/docs/quickstart.md): Install goalify and run it, step by step.
- [Honest limits](https://github.com/Aboudjem/goalify/blob/main/docs/limits.md): Everything goalify does not promise, including that a stopped `/goal` run is not proof of completion.
- [Running it under Codex](https://github.com/Aboudjem/goalify/blob/main/docs/codex.md): The same condition under Codex, and which directives do not carry over.
- [FAQ](https://github.com/Aboudjem/goalify/blob/main/docs/faq.md): Common questions about the two artifacts and the run.
- [LICENSE (MIT)](https://github.com/Aboudjem/goalify/blob/main/LICENSE): Permissive MIT license.

## Install

goalify ships as a Claude Code plugin (in the 10x marketplace) and as a drop-in skill. Either way you
get `/goalify`, which authors the run; you start it with Claude Code's built-in `/goal <condition>`
command (Claude Code 2.1.139+, https://code.claude.com/docs/en/goal).

- [Plugin (recommended)](https://github.com/Aboudjem/goalify#install): `claude plugin marketplace add Aboudjem/10x` then `claude plugin install goalify@10x`.
- [Manual / skill-only](https://github.com/Aboudjem/goalify#install): `git clone https://github.com/Aboudjem/goalify`, then copy `skills/goalify` into `~/.claude/skills/`. Then say "goalify this: <task>" in Claude Code.
